Does the conclusion depend on what counts as "hot"?

Source: R/threshold_sensitivity.R
threshold_sensitivity.Rd

Repeats the before-and-after comparison of summarise_periods() for a range of temperature thresholds. If the later period has more hot days at every threshold, the conclusion does not hinge on one arbitrary cut-off; if it only appears at one threshold, it deserves caution.

Usage

threshold_sensitivity(
  data = melbheat::melb_temp,
  variable = c("tmax", "tmin"),
  thresholds = NULL,
  months = 1:12,
  split_year = 2000,
  min_coverage = 0.8
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the columns year, month and the column named in variable. Defaults to melb_temp.

variable

Which temperature to use: "tmax" (daily maximum, hot days) or "tmin" (daily minimum, hot nights).

thresholds

Numeric vector of thresholds in degrees Celsius. By default 25 to 40 for "tmax" and 12 to 26 for "tmin", in steps of 1.

months

Integer vector of months to include, 1 (January) to 12 (December). Defaults to the whole year. Years are calendar years, so a summer spanning December to February is split across two years.

split_year

A single year. Years <= split_year form the earlier period and years after it the later period.

min_coverage

A number between 0 and 1. A year is marked reliable when the share of days in the chosen months with an observation is at least this value.

Value

A data frame with one row per threshold and columns threshold, mean_before, mean_after (average days per year in each period), n_before, n_after (reliable years used), difference (mean_after - mean_before) and ratio (mean_after / mean_before, NA when the earlier average is 0). The settings are kept in attr(, "settings").

See also

plot_sensitivity() to draw the result.

Examples

sens <- threshold_sensitivity(thresholds = c(30, 35, 40), split_year = 2000)
sens
#>   threshold mean_before mean_after n_before n_after difference    ratio
#> 1        30  28.8333333  36.571429       30      21   7.738095 1.268373
#> 2        35   8.2000000  11.761905       30      21   3.561905 1.434379
#> 3        40   0.8333333   2.428571       30      21   1.595238 2.914286
